title: Is each coffee mix regular, strong or light?
description: Five coffee mixes are each compared with regular coffee by dividing decoction by milk. A mix with a larger share than regular is strong, a smaller share is light, and the same share is regular.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the decoction for each millilitre of milk with the regular share of three sevenths. Watch for students who compare only the amount of decoction.

video_script.why: The child uses the decoction for each millilitre of milk to sort five mixes against regular coffee.
video_script.substitution: Divide the decoction by the milk for each mix and compare the result with three sevenths.
video_script.anchor: Laksh's coffee counter with five tumblers and the regular mix of 15 mL decoction to 35 mL milk
video_script.payoff_line: Two mixes are strong, two are light, and one is regular.

final_answer.spoken: three hundred to six hundred is strong, one hundred fifty to five hundred is light, two hundred to four hundred is strong, twenty four to fifty six is regular, and one hundred to three hundred is light

video_script.fraction_reading: three sevenths, one half, three tenths, one third

names.Laksh: runs the coffee shop and mixes regular, strong and light filter coffee

hold_back: Answer: 300 : 600 strong, 150 : 500 light, 200 : 400 strong, 24 : 56 regular, 100 : 300 light
maths_rules: regular: 15 : 35 = 3 : 7; decoction for each mL of milk 15 ÷ 35 = 3/7, about 0.43
24 : 56: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so 3 : 7, the same as regular
video_script.design: One idea: decoction for each millilitre of milk, compared with regular. Uses the coffee example of the solved video. The five mixes stay for the whole video.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about filter coffee.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Laksh mixes decoction with milk in five ways.
<bookmark mark='dec'/>Decoction means the strong dark liquid made from coffee powder.
<bookmark mark='reg'/>Regular coffee is fifteen millilitres of decoction with thirty five of milk.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is each of the five mixes regular, strong or light?

beats.on_screen: the six tumblers hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the regular tumbler with an arrow marked decoction ÷ milk giving 3/7; a line with strong to the right of 3/7 and light to the left

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the same way as the example in your book, now for five mixes.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide the decoction by the milk for each mix.
<bookmark mark='line'/>A larger share than regular is strong, and a smaller share is light.

beats.on_screen: Given: regular 15 : 35; mixes 300 : 600, 150 : 500, 200 : 400, 24 : 56, 100 : 300 (decoction : milk, in mL)

marks.reg: the regular mix is written first
marks.mix: the five mixes are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='reg'/>Given, regular is fifteen to thirty five.
<bookmark mark='mix'/>The mixes are three hundred to six hundred, and one hundred fifty to five hundred.
<bookmark mark='mix2'/>Also two hundred to four hundred, twenty four to fifty six, and one hundred to three hundred.

beats.on_screen: To find: whether each mix is regular, strong or light

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find whether each mix is regular, strong or light.
<bookmark mark='r'/>Step one, find the share for regular coffee.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Fifteen divided by thirty five is three sevenths. That is about zero point four three.

marks.a: 300 ÷ 600 = 1/2 = 0.5 is written with the word strong
marks.b: 200 ÷ 400 = 1/2 is written with the word strong

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, three hundred divided by six hundred is one half, which is zero point five.
That is more than regular, so this mix is strong.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Two hundred divided by four hundred is also one half, so that mix is strong too.

beats.on_screen: 150 : 500 gives 3/10 = 0.3, less than 0.43, light. 100 : 300 gives 1/3, about 0.33, light

marks.a: 150 ÷ 500 = 3/10 = 0.3 is written with the word light
marks.b: 100 ÷ 300 = 1/3, about 0.33 is written with the word light

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, one hundred fifty divided by five hundred is three tenths, which is zero point three.
That is less than regular, so this mix is light.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One hundred divided by three hundred is one third, about zero point three three.
That mix is light too.

marks.r: 3 : 7 is matched with the regular mix and the word regular is written

narration: <bookmark mark='w'/>Step four, divide twenty four and fifty six by eight to get three and seven.
<bookmark mark='r'/>That is three to seven, the same as regular, so this mix is regular.

marks.chk: the words Check: same denominator are written
marks.half: 1/2 = 7/14 is written beside 3/7 = 6/14 and 7/14 glows as larger
marks.third: 1/3 = 7/21 is written beside 3/7 = 9/21 and 7/21 shows as smaller

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check by writing the shares with the same denominator.
<bookmark mark='half'/>One half is seven fourteenths. Three sevenths is six fourteenths, so one half is more.
<bookmark mark='third'/>One third is seven twenty firsts. Three sevenths is nine twenty firsts, so one third is less.
